question: If AI helps solve a famous maths problem, how should we share the credit and check the result?
reflection: When machines help open old puzzles, people can spend more of their curiosity on the next questions worth asking.

sources.subject: 64 parallel subagents just ended a 50-year math standoff

one_line: OpenAI says a GPT-5.6 model using 64 parallel helpers produced a proof of a 50-year-old maths conjecture in under an hour, though experts have not yet checked it.

top_stories.title: AI proof of a 50-year-old maths problem
top_stories.what: OpenAI says GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, running 64 subagents in parallel, produced a proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture in under an hour and published the prompt, the proof and a machine-checkable version.
top_stories.why: If confirmed, it shows how multi-agent AI can attack hard open problems, a pattern that could later apply to policy and research questions.

top_stories.title: Cursor adds side chats and searchable history
top_stories.what: Cursor 3.11 lets users search all past agent conversations and open side chats for quick tangents without disturbing the main thread.
top_stories.why: Keeping a searchable record of agent work helps teams audit and reuse what AI produced.

top_stories.title: Song to sheet music, per instrument
top_stories.what: Kyutai released an open model that turns a song into separate MIDI tracks for each instrument.
top_stories.why: Music transcription tools could support music education and the preservation of local musical heritage.

top_stories.title: Cleaner web addresses for AI-built apps
top_stories.what: Google AI Studio now lets people give deployed apps a custom name under its own domain.
top_stories.why: Small polish like this makes quick AI prototypes easier to share with stakeholders.

saudi_lens.text: Open music transcription models could help Saudi cultural bodies document and teach traditional music, provided they are tested on regional instruments and rhythms.

idea.title: Heritage music archive pilot
idea.pitch: Test whether open transcription tools can turn recordings of traditional performances into notation for teaching and archiving.
idea.first_step: Choose three short public-domain recordings and compare the tool's output with a musician's transcription.

idea_kids.title: Loops and paths puzzle book
idea_kids.pitch: A puzzle book where children draw closed loops on simple maps so every road is used exactly twice, introducing graph puzzles through play.
idea_kids.first_step: Draw ten small maps of dots and lines, from easy to hard, and test them with two children.
